graph.provenance: An extract of the graph, in text, holding only what these 24 projections touch: every canonical entity any recorded set names, and every alias row pointing at one. It is here so the fixture can be RE-PROJECTED rather than trusted — `tests/test_skill_entity_overlap.py` builds a store from it and checks the recorded sets byte for byte — and so the eval never has to open the live store, which `KGStore(path)` provisions on open and a test must not be the thing that writes to. Read-only from $HOME/lloyd-data/_pipeline/vault-derived/kg.sqlite, 2026-10-08; the 14,305 mention edges and 13,766 entities that are not these 24 skills' subjects are deliberately not here, and cannot be: the store is 64 MB.

provenance.entity_sets: `entity_sets` are the canonical entity names the PRODUCTION store ($HOME/lloyd-data/_pipeline/vault-derived/kg.sqlite) resolved from each side's SKILL.md body on 2026-10-08, with the harness-tool and path screens on. They are recorded rather than recomputed so the eval scores the corpus the labels were adjudicated against; `fixture_drift` is what compares them against live bytes, and prints, on every run.
provenance.incumbent_disagreement: Why a stability clause exists: the 2026-10-07 pass scored ml-paper-writing vs research-paper-writing at 0.03 and called them name look-alikes; the 2026-10-08 pass scored the same pair 0.327-0.358 and filed it as #2409. #2409 records it verbatim: 'The two numbers are not comparable and one of the two readings is wrong.' A tokenisation-dependent score is not a metric, which is the defect this fixture's stability test is written against.
provenance.incumbent_figure_note: The scores quoted above are the 2026-10-08 pass's own, produced by an improvised tokenisation that is the defect #2409 records ('The two numbers are not comparable and one of the two readings is wrong'). This scorer's `desc_jaccard` is committed and reproducible; on these pairs it reproduces the same ordering, not the same decimals.
provenance.negatives: Negatives reconstructed on 2026-10-08 from the pairs autonomy run #83's Stage 5 screen flagged and #2409's triage named as 'name look-alikes with disjoint objects': the three coding-CLI pairs it quotes by name and score, the six github-* pairs that clear the incumbent's own 0.34 threshold (this scorer reproduces the 0.34-0.46 band #2409 quotes for that cluster), and the deliberate Stage-1/Stage-2 analysis/write split it names. The pass reported 11 flagged pairs = 1 real + 10 look-alikes, so 10 is what the record supports; the 11th flagged pair was never named in either artifact and none is invented here.
provenance.positives: #2409 (ml-paper-writing / research-paper-writing) and #2287 (memory-capture / periodic-memory-capture-lloyd), both adjudicated by a human reading the two skills, not by a score.
provenance.screen_precision: The instrument this fixture judges: autonomy task #83's Stage 5 description screen flagged 11 pairs ≥ 0.34 on 2026-10-08 and exactly one was a real scope duplicate, so precision on that night is 1/12 (1 real of 12 flagged pairs counting the pair the screen itself called real). The 11 named false positives are the negatives in this file.
provenance.text_source: Each row's `descriptions` are the front-matter descriptions of ~/obsidian/skills/<name>/SKILL.md as read on 2026-10-08; `research-paper-writing` and `periodic-memory-capture-lloyd` are read from the archived tree, since both went `status: archived` when their folds landed and `iter_active_skills()` no longer yields them. The bodies those entity sets were projected from are the same files at the same date.
provenance.why_dated: Hand-adjudicated ground truth rots. The 2026-09-20 class rule says a hand-maintained allowlist cannot close a property over an open-set corpus, so this is an eval fixture with a date and a provenance, not a permanent exemption table: it is evidence about the scorer, and a scorer's ranking is reported, never gated on it.
